legend: Anup was working tirelessly to finalize the problem set for the upcoming Insomnia contest. Meanwhile, Darsh, having absolutely nothing better to do, wandered over to demand a treat(chapo in local lingo). Hoping to get back to work, Anup struck a deal: Darsh would get his chapo, but only if he could first solve a seemingly innocent, yet "not-so-simple" problem.
Anup describes a process to build a tree:

Given an integer n%%ZSMJ0%%, construct an array a[a1,a2,…,an]%%ZSMJ1%% of size n%%ZSMJ2%% consisting of zeroes and ones where a1=0%%ZSMJ3%%. Consider a tree with n+1%%ZSMJ4%% vertices labeled 0,1,2,…,n%%ZSMJ5%%, where vertex 0%%ZSMJ6%% is designated as the root.
ai=0%%ZSMJ8%%, add an edge between vertex i%%ZSMJ9%% and vertex i−1%%ZSMJ10%%;
ai=1%%ZSMJ11%%, add an edge between vertex i%%ZSMJ12%% and vertex i−2%%ZSMJ13%%.

Let h(a)%%ZSMJ14%% be the height of the tree for one possible valid array a%%ZSMJ15%%. Anup asks Darsh to find the sum of h(a)%%ZSMJ16%% over all possible valid arrays of 0%%ZSMJ17%%s and 1%%ZSMJ18%%s where a1=0%%ZSMJ19%%. Since this sum can be incredibly large, output the answer modulo 109+7%%ZSMJ20%%.
input: The first line contains a single integer t%%ZSMJ21%% (1≤t≤104%%ZSMJ22%%) — the number of test cases.
The only line of each test case contains a single integer n%%ZSMJ23%% (1≤n≤2⋅105%%ZSMJ24%%) — the size of the array.
output: For each test case, output a single integer — the sum of the heights of the trees formed by all valid arrays, modulo 109+7%%ZSMJ25%%.
